findings.title: `include_website_name` missing the `?` suffix breaks conditional inclusion
findings.body: Every other manually-defined inclusion guard in this file follows the `include_#{attr}?` naming convention (e.g. `include_email?`, `include_card_image_badge_id?`, `include_card_image_badge?`, `include_suspend_reason?`), and the `untrusted_attributes`/`private_attributes` macros generate methods named with the trailing `?` as well. The newly added method is defined as `def include_website_name` (no `?`), so the serializer framework never calls it to decide whether to include the `website_name` attribute. As a result, `website_name` is unconditionally serialized for every user (even when `website` is blank, producing a `website_name: null` entry), instead of being gated by `website.present?` as intended.

findings.title: `website_name` is not covered by the `website` untrusted-attribute restriction, leaking site info to low-trust/anonymous viewers
findings.body: `:website` is listed in `untrusted_attributes`, which hides it from anonymous viewers of TL0 users via `scope.restrict_user_fields?`. The new derived field `website_name` (added at line 43/137) is computed from the same `website` data but is not included in that `untrusted_attributes` list, and its own gate (`include_website_name`, see separate finding) never checks `scope.restrict_user_fields?`. Consequently, even when the raw `website` value is correctly hidden for a restricted viewer, the derived `website_name` (hostname or hostname+path) is still exposed in the API response, leaking information the attribute list was designed to protect.

findings.title: Untrusted-attribute test does not cover the new `website_name` field
findings.body: The `untrusted_attributes` array used by the "with a TL0 user seen as anonymous" spec (`%i{bio_raw bio_cooked bio_excerpt location website profile_background card_background}`) was not updated to include `:website_name`. Since `website_name` is derived from the restricted `website` field but is not actually hidden for untrusted/anonymous viewers (see related bug in `user_serializer.rb`), this test gives false confidence that sensitive website data is properly hidden; it does not fail despite the leak.
